candidate_assessment.evidence: wait_for_beep awaits the tenant event which beep_agent sets; suspended receiver regressions and scheduled-boundary cases passed.

Second beep_swarm raises RuntimeError before replacing payload, including same-value and falsy payload cases. Retained first pulse for repeated/late waits remains intentional; this is not a reusable queue.

independent_checks.name: Cancellation after unicast emission preserves payload for replacement
Cancelling first awakened same-tenant consumer lets second consume once
Broadcast remains available after awakened consumer cancellation
64 concurrent same-tenant waiters consume 64 separately scheduled unicasts exactly once
Mixed fanout with 512 tenants and current/late/repeated receivers
Deregistration after pending signal rejects all old waiters and prevents payload crossing registration
Falsy/None broadcast payloads survive fanout and second emission rejects before state change
Unicast after broadcast is consumed before retained global pulse
Scheduled unicast around event wait boundary has no lost wakeup
Repeated registration/deregistration keeps counts consistent and unknown tenant unicast does not leak
Independent scenarios leave no pending asyncio tasks

supporting_source_checks.observation: Identity check, payload consumption and event clear are synchronous; no await under RLock and no task yield before entering Event.wait.
Deregistration removes payload and sets old event to wake waiters; identity prevents crossing a new registration.
Unicast sets the same per-tenant event; broadcast rejects second emission before mutation and sets all registered events.
Scoped consumer creates a fresh pager and issues one global broadcast.

official_documentation.observation: Event.set wakes all current waiters; clear affects subsequent waits; Event is not thread-safe.

limitations: All exercised calls ran on one event-loop thread, as required by the class contract; no cross-thread safety claim.
The existing unicast mailbox retains only one pending payload per tenant; bursts without consumption can overwrite earlier values. This behavior predates the fix and no FIFO guarantee is introduced.
Fanout coverage is bounded and supports delivery behavior, not advertised latency or million-agent scaling. Event fanout cost also depends on total waiting tasks when multiple waiters share a tenant.
No protected native runtime, operator data, filesystem database, remote effects or external swarm was executed. Only source/tests/evidence files were read and this report written.
Repeated waits after broadcast intentionally return the retained pulse; callers needing another round must create a new pager.
